title: 19th Annual Pershing Square Value Investing and Philanthropy Challenge
description: 19th Annual Pershing Square Value Investing and Philanthropy Challenge
summary: The speaker argues that Baker Hughes is a compelling compounder poised to transform into a service-based industrial energy technology business with significant margin expansion potential. In the beverage sector, the talk highlights Celsius Energy as an undervalued growth opportunity within the sugar-free category, noting its strong market position and potential for margin improvement. Conversely, the speaker expresses skepticism regarding Uber's ability to disrupt the US delivery duopoly and dismisses Tesla's prospects in autonomous delivery, while viewing Costco's grocery market exposure as having limited competitive threat from Instacart.

claims.claim: The speaker argues the market is undervaluing Celsius Energy's growth potential and believes the company can exceed market standards by 400 basis points in the medium-term.
claims.quote: Celsius Energy is the third largest energy drink company in the US today after Red Bull and Monster. It has two main brands, Celsius and Alan. The market today is undervaluing its growth potential and we believe that we can exceed growth by the market standards by 400 bips in the medium-term

claims.claim: The speaker notes that Celsius trades at a forward PE multiple of 22x, which is lower than what Monster Energy has ever traded at, even during the financial crisis.
claims.quote: On a valuation standpoint the company's trading at a 22x forward PE multiple today a number that even Monster Energy has never traded at even during the great financial crisis on an absolute level

claims.claim: The speaker states that Celsius is the largest sugar-free energy drinking company in the US with a 34% market share.
claims.quote: Celsius energy is the largest sugar-free energy drinking company in the US today with a 34% market share.

claims.claim: The speaker asserts that today Celsius and Alani are established brands with $1.3 billion in revenue each and a 10% market share.
claims.quote: Today Celsius and Alani both are established brands having reached escape velocity in the segment at $1.3 billion in revenue each with a 10% market share.

claims.claim: The speaker believes that in the sugar-free category today, Celsius is number one because of the Celsius and Alani blend together.
claims.quote: Number one, in Sugarfly today, Celsius is number one because of the Celsius and the Alani blend together. They've already beaten Monster and Monster is in fact losing share.

claims.claim: The speaker estimates that operating margins can expand a total of 300 basis points in the medium-term.
claims.quote: operating margins to expand a total of 300 bibs and at a multiple correction to levels before the private label issue, we get an IL of 25%.

claims.claim: The speaker models a base case where the company achieves $4.1 billion of topline at an 18% growth rate.
claims.quote: in our base case, we achieved the company to be at $4.1 billion of topline at an 18% growth rate, lost margins to expand 200 bibs from today's position, operating margins to expand a total of 300 bibs

claims.claim: The speaker views Baker Hughes as a compounder with significant upside potential due to its role in the energy value chain and a shift towards a service-based revenue model.
claims.quote: We have found that this has created an asymmetric long opportunity in Baker Hughes with three 63% upside potential over the next three years. Our work has found that the market underappreciates the role Baker Hughes plays in the energy value chain

claims.claim: Baker Hughes is expected to transform into a business resembling a 'seaman's energy' or 'G Vernova' by 2028, with over 60% of revenue coming from industrial energy technology.
claims.quote: Our work has found that by 2028 over 60% of this business's revenue will come from industrial energy technology. This transforms Baker Hughes into a business that will increasingly look like a seaman's energy or a G Vernova

claims.claim: The speaker forecasts a margin expansion of 550 basis points over the next five years as Baker shifts towards a service-based revenue model.
claims.quote: So ultimately, the shift towards a service-based revenue model materially lifts Baker's margin. We forecast 550 bips of expansion in the next five years. And I just want to point out that this margin is durable through inflation.

claims.claim: The speaker views the US delivery market as a stable duopoly where Door Dash has gained significantly more market share than Uber over the last five years.
claims.quote: essentially in the US we view this as a semistable duopoly. So if you go back to this chart shows market share from 2021 through 2025 Uber's share was 30. It's grown to 32 over the 5 years. Door Dash's share was 55 to 63 over those five years.

claims.claim: The speaker acknowledges that Uber is a high-quality winner in many areas, even in international markets where it competes with Door Dash.
claims.quote: in international most markets where Door Dash go head-to-head with Uber, we think Door Dash has gained more share or rather Fault and Deliveroo or Deliveroo is early, but in the six months of ownership, Deliveroo's gained share we believe. claims.claim: The speaker believes autonomous delivery will not scale in the forecast period and that Tesla would need years to disrupt Door Dash's three-sided network.
claims.quote: So, we don't believe that autonomous um like delivery really scales in our forecast period from 2026 to 2029. Um we believe in the outy years that it benefits Door Dash materially. Um, we just believe that there's a three-sided network and there's stuff in the physical world that happens that's really tough to replicate and that uh like at Tesla um they would just have to do so much and it's going to take years and years to disrupt that three-sided network.
